transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Thank you for being here. As you know, the district's middle-school mathematics assessment is scheduled for May 14, 2027, and I've asked each of you to review the draft administration plan before I give it final approval. The plan currently calls for digital testing on school tablets, all 26 students testing together in Room 201, one proctor, graphing calculators available throughout the assessment, and completed materials stored in the general records cabinet. I'd like to go through each component and hear your feedback. Let's start with the testing setup and logistics — does anyone see any concerns with the room arrangement, proctoring, or technology?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to flag a concern with the room arrangement. My finalized roster has 26 students, but the state administration manual limits a testing room to 14 students. I've already prepared Room 201 for 14 students and Room 202 for the remaining 12 students to comply with that requirement. However, I should note that this updated room plan has not yet been entered into the district tracker, so the draft plan still reflects all 26 students in Room 201.

transcript.text: I need to flag a concern with the calculator policy in the draft plan. While reviewing the current state mathematics assessment manual this week, I found that calculators may be used only on section 2 of the assessment, and they must be four-function calculators — not graphing calculators. The draft plan currently calls for graphing calculators to be available throughout the entire assessment, which would not comply with the state manual. I have not yet amended the draft plan to reflect this.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I need to flag a critical technology concern. My device test found that the 26 assigned tablets cannot run the required secure testing application, and we cannot obtain compatible devices before May 14. I contacted the assessment vendor, and they confirmed that paper booklets are authorized for this administration. However, this result has not yet been added to the draft plan, which still calls for digital testing on school tablets.
transcript.speaker: A4

transcript.text: I need to flag a security concern with the storage plan. My security review of the state testing agreement, which I completed this week, requires that completed assessment materials be sealed in tamper-evident envelopes and stored in a locked cabinet for exactly 30 calendar days. The draft plan currently calls for completed materials to be stored in the general records cabinet, which does not meet these requirements. I have not yet updated the storage field in the draft plan to reflect the correct procedures.
transcript.speaker: A5

transcript.text: Thank you all for these critical findings. Let me summarize what I'm hearing: First, Mr. Bell, the state manual limits testing rooms to 14 students, so we need to split into Room 201 for 14 and Room 202 for 12, and that needs to be updated in the tracker. Second, Ms. Shah, calculators may only be used on section 2 and must be four-function, not graphing — so the draft plan needs to be corrected on both the calculator type and the timing. Third, Mr. Nguyen, since the tablets can't run the secure testing app and we can't get compatible devices before May 14, we need to switch to paper booklets, which the vendor has authorized. And fourth, Ms. Delgado, completed materials must be sealed in tamper-evident envelopes and stored in a locked cabinet for exactly 30 calendar days — not in the general records cabinet. Each of you has identified a serious compliance issue with the current draft. Before I settle on the revised plan, I have one question: Mr. Bell, with the room split into two rooms, will we need a second proctor, or can one proctor manage both rooms? And Mr. Nguyen, will the paper booklets require any changes to the calculator or storage procedures we've just discussed?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: Dr. Morris, to your first question: yes, we will need a second proctor. The state administration manual limits a testing room to 14 students, and with 14 students in Room 201 and 12 in Room 202, each room requires its own proctor to maintain proper supervision and compliance. One proctor cannot simultaneously monitor two separate rooms. I'll make sure the updated two-room, two-proctor plan gets entered into the district tracker. As for your question about whether paper booklets affect the calculator or storage procedures, I'll defer to Ms. Shah and Ms. Delgado on those points, since those fall under their areas of expertise.
